title: 20 Common English Grammar Mistakes
excerpt: Learn 20 common English grammar mistakes with simple examples and clear explanations to improve your speaking and writing skills.
plainContent: English grammar can be confusing, especially when two words or sentence structures look almost the same. Some mistakes are very common because people hear or use them in everyday conversation. The good news is that most of these mistakes are easy to fix once you understand the rule. Here are some common English grammar mistakes, with simple explanations and examples. 1. I Wish I Was vs. I Wish I Were When you talk about an unreal or imaginary situation, use “were” in formal English. Common: I wish I was a cat. Better in formal English: I wish I were a cat. Why? The sentence describes something that is not true. This is called the subjunctive mood. More examples: I wish I were taller. I wish she were here. If I were you, I would study harder. In everyday conversation, “I wish I was” is also widely used, but “I wish I were” is the safer choice for formal writing and exams. 2. Giving an Exam vs. Taking an Exam Students often say: Incorrect in standard English: I gave an exam yesterday. Correct: I took an exam yesterday. A student takes or sits for an exam. A teacher gives , sets , or administers an exam. For example: I took my English exam yesterday. The teacher gave us an English exam. She is preparing to sit for her final exam. 3. Enter vs. Enter Into The verb “enter” already means “go into,” so we normally do not use “to” after it when talking about entering a place. Incorrect: We entered into the classroom. Correct: We entered the classroom. However, “enter into” is correct when it has a different meaning. For example: The two companies entered into an agreement. They entered into a discussion about the problem. So, remember: Enter + place Enter into + agreement, discussion, contract, etc. 4. Using “The” Before General Nouns and Languages Do not use “the” before a material or substance when you are talking about it in general. Incorrect: The gold is a precious metal. Correct: Gold is a precious metal. We also do not normally use “the” before the name of a language. Incorrect: He speaks the English. Correct: He speaks English. More examples: Water is important for life. Silver is a useful metal. She speaks Bengali and English. There are exceptions. For example, “the English” can refer to English people as a group. 5. Returned vs. Returned Back “Return” already means “go or come back,” so “back” is usually unnecessary. Incorrect: She returned back to school. Correct: She returned to school. You can also say: She went back to school. She came back to school. Do not use “returned back” when “returned” already expresses the meaning you need. 6. Between vs. Among A common rule says to use “between” for two things and “among” for three or more. This is useful for beginners, but it is not the complete rule. “Between” is generally used when we are talking about separate, clearly identified people or things. It can be used with more than two. Examples: The agreement was between Bangladesh, India, and Nepal. The money was divided between the three brothers. “Among” is usually used when people or things are considered as part of a group. Examples: She was sitting among her friends. The teacher distributed the books among the students. For Class 10 students, remember that “between” often focuses on individual relationships, while “among” focuses on a group. 7. Then vs. Than “Than” is used when making a comparison. Incorrect: I would rather have cake then ice cream. Correct: I would rather have cake than ice cream. “Then” is usually related to time or sequence. Examples: She is taller than me. This book is better than that one. We finished our homework and then watched television. A simple trick: Than = comparison Then = time or next step 8. Fewer vs. Less Use “fewer” with countable nouns. Use “less” with uncountable nouns. Incorrect: I have less books than you. Correct: I have fewer books than you. Examples: There are fewer students in the class today. I have fewer problems now. I need less water. We have less time. You can count books, students, and apples. You cannot normally count water, time, or sugar as individual units. So: Fewer + countable nouns Less + uncountable nouns 9. Its vs. It's These two words have different meanings. Its shows possession. It's is a short form of “it is” or “it has.” Incorrect: The cat licked it's paw. Correct: The cat licked its paw. Examples: The dog hurt its leg. The company changed its policy. It's raining. It's been a long day. A useful test is to replace “it's” with “it is” or “it has.” If the sentence still makes sense, “it's” may be correct. 10. Avoid Double Negatives in Standard English A double negative happens when two negative words are used in the same clause. Non-standard: I don't need no help. Standard: I don't need any help. You can also say: I need no help. In some dialects and informal varieties of English, double negatives are used intentionally. However, they are generally avoided in formal English and academic writing. 11. Who vs.

title: Tense in English Grammar: A Complete Guide for Beginners
excerpt: If you say “I eat,” “I ate,” “I am eating,” and “I will eat,” the main verb changes the way your listener understands time, action, and context. That is the basic idea behind tense . Tense is one of …
plainContent: If you say “I eat,” “I ate,” “I am eating,” and “I will eat,” the main verb changes the way your listener understands time, action, and context. That is the basic idea behind tense . Tense is one of the most important parts of English grammar because it helps us explain when something happens, whether an action is finished, whether it is continuing, and how one event relates to another . For beginners, however, English tenses can feel unnecessarily complicated. You may hear about 12 tenses, memorize formulas, and still hesitate when choosing between sentences such as: I went to school. I was going to school. I have gone to school. I had gone to school. I will go to school. The good news is that you do not need to memorize dozens of rules without understanding them. Once you understand the relationship between time and aspect , English tenses become much easier. In this guide, we will explain what tense means, the commonly taught 12 English tenses, when to use each one, practical examples, common mistakes, and a simple method for learning them. What Is Tense in English Grammar? Tense is a grammatical form of a verb used to indicate the time of an action, event, or state. Cambridge Dictionary defines tense as a form of a verb that shows the time at which an action happened. For example, “I sing” is present tense, while “I sang” is past tense. Consider these sentences: I study English. I studied English yesterday. I will study English tomorrow. The verb forms help us understand the time being discussed. study → present studied → past will study → future form There is an important technical point here. In linguistic terms, English has only two grammatical tenses marked directly on the verb: present and past . English expresses future time through structures such as will , be going to , and present-tense forms used for future situations. The British Council and Cambridge Dictionary both explain this distinction. However, English-learning textbooks commonly teach 12 tenses , combining tense with aspect and time. This traditional system is extremely useful for beginners, so we will use it throughout this guide. Why Is Tense Important in English? Imagine someone tells you: “I eat dinner.” You understand that eating is presented as a present or habitual action. Now compare: “I ate dinner.” The action happened in the past. And: “I am eating dinner.” The action is currently in progress. The difference is small in vocabulary but significant in meaning. Tense helps you communicate: when an action happens whether an action is finished whether an action is continuing whether an action happened before another event whether something is planned or expected how long an action has continued This matters in everyday conversation, academic writing, professional communication, storytelling, examinations, and English proficiency tests. A sentence with the wrong tense can change the meaning completely. Example I live in Dhaka. This normally describes your current situation. I lived in Dhaka. This normally suggests that you lived there in the past and may not live there now. The tense gives the listener important information without requiring additional explanation. The Basic Idea Behind English Tenses Before learning the 12 commonly taught tenses, understand two concepts: Time Aspect 1. Time English grammar commonly discusses three time references: Present Past Future 2. Aspect Aspect describes how an action relates to time. The four commonly taught aspects are: Simple : an action or state viewed generally Continuous : an action in progress Perfect : an action viewed in relation to another time Perfect continuous : emphasizes duration or ongoing activity in relation to another time When these concepts are combined, we get the familiar 12-tense framework. Time Simple Continuous Perfect Perfect Continuous Present Present Simple Present Continuous Present Perfect Present Perfect Continuous Past Past Simple Past Continuous Past Perfect Past Perfect Continuous Future Future Simple Future Continuous Future Perfect Future Perfect Continuous Do not try to memorize this table immediately. Instead, understand what each pattern means. The 12 English Tenses Explained 1. Present Simple Tense The present simple is used for things that happen regularly, facts, general truths, routines, and permanent or relatively stable situations. Structure Subject + base verb For third-person singular subjects such as he, she, and it , the verb usually takes -s or -es . Examples I work every day. You study English. They play football. She works in a bank. He watches television at night. The sun rises in the east. When to use the present simple Use it for: Habits I drink tea every morning. Regular activities She goes to university by bus. Facts Water boils at 100°C at standard atmospheric pressure. General truths Practice improves your skills. Permanent or long-term situations He lives in Bangladesh. Common time expressions always usually often sometimes rarely

title: How to Write an Application: Format and Examples
excerpt: Learn how to write applications with simple formats and examples for leave, testimonial, transcript, study tour, SSC, HSC, university, and jobs.
plainContent: Application writing is an important part of English writing in Bangladesh. Students may need to write an application to the headmaster, principal, department head, or another authority for different reasons. For example, you may need to write an application for leave, a testimonial, a transfer certificate, permission for a study tour, or another school or college matter. University students and job seekers also write formal applications for academic and professional purposes. The good news is that most formal applications follow a simple structure. Once you understand the format, you can write an application for almost any situation. This guide explains the basic application writing format and provides examples for school, college, university, and job applications. What Is an Application? An application is a formal written request made to a person or authority. For example: A student writes to the headmaster for leave. A student writes to the principal for a testimonial. A university student writes to the examination office for a transcript. A student writes to an authority for permission to join a study tour. A job seeker writes to an employer to apply for a position. The purpose of an application should be clear from the beginning. Avoid unnecessary information and explain exactly what you are requesting. Basic Application Writing Format A formal application usually contains these parts: Date Name and designation of the recipient Institution or organisation Address Subject Salutation Main body Closing Name and identifying information of the applicant A simple structure looks like this: Date The [Designation] [Institution Name] [Address] Subject: Application for [purpose]. Sir/Madam, First paragraph: Introduce yourself and explain why you are writing. Second paragraph: Give the necessary details about your situation. Final paragraph: Clearly state what you are requesting. Yours faithfully/obediently, [Your Name] [Class/Department] [Roll/ID] The exact format can vary between institutions, so students should follow any specific instructions given by their school, college, university, or employer. 1. Application for Leave A leave application is written when you need permission to remain absent from school, college, or another institution. Example: Leave Application for Illness 15 January 2026 The Headmaster Ideal High School Motijheel, Dhaka Subject: Application for leave of absence. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am a student of Class IX, Section B, of your school. I have been suffering from a high fever for the last three days, and the doctor has advised me to take rest. For this reason, I will not be able to attend school from 15 January to 18 January 2026. I therefore request you to kindly grant me leave for these four days. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Yours obediently, Md. Rakib Hasan Class IX, Section B Roll No. 17 What to include in a leave application Make sure you mention: The reason for your absence The dates of your leave Your class or department Your roll or student ID Any supporting document if the institution requires one Do not write a long explanation. Give only the information the authority needs. 2. Application for a Testimonial A testimonial is an official document that may provide information about a student's academic record, conduct, or period of study at an institution. Students may need a testimonial after completing SSC or HSC or when applying for further education or other purposes. Example: Testimonial Application 10 February 2026 The Principal Dhaka College New Market, Dhaka Subject: Application for a testimonial. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I passed the HSC examination in 2025 from your college under the Dhaka Education Board. I am now preparing to apply for higher studies and require a testimonial from the college. I therefore request you to kindly issue me a testimonial at your earliest convenience. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Yours obediently, Sumaiya Akter HSC 2025, Science Group Roll No. 124356 Tip for students If the institution has a specific testimonial form, use that form instead of writing a separate application. Some Bangladeshi institutions provide their own testimonial forms with fields for student information and academic details. 3. Application for an Academic Transcript University students may need an academic transcript when applying for higher studies, scholarships, employment, or other official purposes. The procedure is different from one university to another. Some universities require a specific form, fee payment, clearance, or supporting documents. Example 22 March 2026 The Controller of Examinations University of Dhaka Dhaka-1000 Subject: Application for issuance of academic transcript. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I completed my Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science and Engineering from your university in 2025. I now require

title: Top 10 Affordable Countries to Study Abroad for Bangladeshi Students
excerpt: Ranked list of the cheapest study-abroad destinations for Bangladeshi students in 2026, covering tuition, living costs, scholarships, and work rights.
plainContent: Cost is usually the first real obstacle for Bangladeshi students who want to study abroad. Tuition is only part of it — visa fees, accommodation, food, transport, and health insurance can all add up quickly. The good news is that there are still plenty of countries where a serious student from Bangladesh can complete a quality degree without taking on crushing debt. This guide ranks the ten most affordable study-abroad destinations for Bangladeshi students in 2026, based on average annual tuition, living costs, scholarship availability, and post-study work rights. Costs are rough averages — your real budget will depend on the city, the university, and your lifestyle. 1. Germany Public universities in Germany charge no tuition for bachelor's and most master's programmes, even for international students. You only pay a semester contribution of roughly €150–350. Annual living cost in cities like Leipzig, Dresden, or Aachen is around €9,000–11,000. A blocked account of €11,904 is required for the student visa. German universities offer hundreds of English-taught master's programmes in engineering, computer science, and business. 2. Norway Public universities in Norway were free for everyone until 2023, and remain free for EU/EEA students. International students now pay tuition, but it is still moderate (NOK 80,000–250,000 a year depending on the programme). Living costs are higher than Germany, but part-time work rights are generous. 3. Malaysia Malaysia is one of the most popular budget destinations for Bangladeshi students. Tuition at private universities typically runs USD 3,000–6,000 a year, and many UK/Australian universities have branch campuses (Monash, Nottingham, Reading) where you get the same degree at a fraction of the cost. Living expenses in Kuala Lumpur are around USD 4,000–5,000 a year. 4. Hungary The Hungarian government's Stipendium Hungaricum scholarship is one of the most accessible fully funded options for Bangladeshi students. It covers tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, and medical insurance. Even self-funded, Hungary is cheap: tuition is around €1,500–5,000 a year and living costs in Budapest are around €6,000–8,000. 5. Poland Poland has become a quiet favourite. Tuition for English-taught programmes is around €2,000–4,000 a year, and cities like Kraków, Wrocław, and Warsaw offer good infrastructure and a large international student community. Living costs are similar to Hungary. 6. China The Chinese government, provinces, and individual universities offer a huge number of scholarships (CSC, Confucius, Belt & Road) for Bangladeshi students. Self-funded tuition is also cheap — RMB 18,000–35,000 a year. Living costs depend heavily on the city; tier-2 cities like Hefei or Wuhan are very affordable. 7. Russia Russia offers the Open Doors and government scholarships, plus low-cost self-funded study (USD 2,500–6,000 a year). Medical universities in Russia are particularly popular for Bangladeshi students who couldn't get into BMDC-approved colleges at home, though you need to check the latest BMDC recognition list before committing. 8. Turkey The Türkiye Bursları scholarship is fully funded and competitive. Self-funded tuition at Turkish state universities is around USD 500–1,500 a year. Istanbul and Ankara have lower living costs than most European cities. 9. India India is geographically close, culturally familiar, and degrees from top Indian universities (IITs, IIMs, Delhi University, JNU) are well respected. The ICCR scholarship is offered specifically to Bangladeshi students. Self-funded tuition is moderate, and living costs are the lowest on this list. 10. Czech Republic Czech public universities are free if you study in Czech. English-taught programmes cost around €4,000–8,000 a year. Prague offers excellent quality of life and Czech degrees are recognised across the EU. How to choose between them Don't pick a country based only on cost. Consider: Language of instruction — English-taught programmes are easier short-term, but learning the local language unlocks part-time jobs and post-study work. Post-study work rights — Germany gives 18 months, Malaysia 12, Hungary 9. China and Russia are stricter. Field of study — engineering and IT are well represented everywhere; arts and humanities are stronger in Western Europe. IELTS requirement — most of these countries accept IELTS 6.0–6.5. Check your target university's exact requirement and use our IELTS Band Score Calculator to plan your prep. FAQ Which is the cheapest country to study abroad for Bangladeshi students? Germany is the cheapest overall because public-university tuition is free. Hungary, Poland, and Malaysia are close behind if you include scholarships. Can I work part-time while studying in these countries? Yes — most of them allow 20 hours per week during term and full-time during holidays. Earnings depend heavily on the local minimum wage. Do I need IELTS for all of them? Almost always. A

title: Study Tour Application: Format, Tips, and 5 Examples for Students
excerpt: Learn how to write a study tour application with the correct format. Includes 5 examples for school and college students plus simple writing tips.
plainContent: A study tour is an exciting part of student life. It allows students to visit historical places, industries, museums, universities, and different cities. Through these trips, students learn outside the classroom and gain real world knowledge. However, before joining a tour, students usually need to submit a study tour application to their teacher, principal, or department head. This application asks for permission to participate in the tour. In this guide, you will learn what a study tour application is, why schools require it, the proper format, useful writing tips, and several examples you can use as templates. What Is a Study Tour Application? A study tour application is a formal letter written by a student requesting permission to join an educational trip organized by a school, college, or university. The application usually includes: Student information Purpose of the tour Destination Duration of the tour A polite request for permission Educational tours may include visits to museums, cultural places, industries, or universities. For example, students often visit famous educational locations such as the National Museum of Bangladesh or historical places like the Lalbagh Fort to learn about culture and history. Because these tours involve travel and responsibility, institutions require formal permission requests. Why Schools Require a Study Tour Application Schools and colleges request applications for several important reasons. 1. Official Permission The application allows teachers or principals to officially approve your participation in the tour. 2. Student Records Institutions maintain records of students who are attending the trip. 3. Safety and Responsibility If something unexpected happens during the tour, the school has documentation that the student received official permission. 4. Organization Applications help schools manage the number of participants and make better arrangements for transportation and accommodation. Format of a Study Tour Application Writing a proper application is simple when you follow the correct structure. 1. Receiver Information Start by addressing the person responsible for approving the tour. Example: To The Principal / Head Teacher School or College Name 2. Subject Line Clearly mention the purpose of the letter. Example: Subject: Application for permission to join the study tour 3. Salutation Use a polite greeting. Example: Respected Sir/Madam, 4. Body Paragraph Explain your request clearly. Include: Tour destination Tour date Educational purpose 5. Closing End with a polite request and gratitude. Example: I kindly request you to grant me permission to participate in the study tour. 6. Signature Finish with your details. Example: Your name Class or department Roll number Date Example 1: Study Tour Application for School Students To The Principal ABC High School Subject: Application for permission to join the study tour Respected Sir, I respectfully state that our school is organizing a study tour to the National Museum next week. The tour will help students learn more about the history and culture of our country. I am very interested in joining this educational trip with my classmates. It will provide valuable learning experience outside the classroom. Therefore, I kindly request you to grant me permission to participate in the study tour. Thank you for your consideration. Yours obediently Raihan Class: 9 Roll: 12 Date: 16 March 2026 Example 2: Study Tour Application for College Students To The Principal XYZ College Subject: Application for permission to go on a study tour Respected Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that our department has arranged a study tour to a historical site next month. The purpose of this tour is to help students gain practical knowledge related to our academic subjects. I would like to join this tour along with my classmates. I believe the trip will enhance our understanding and provide valuable educational exposure. Therefore, I kindly request you to allow me to participate in the study tour. Yours faithfully Raihan Ahmed Department: History Roll: 24 Date: 16 March 2026 Example 3: Short Study Tour Application To The Head Teacher ABC School Subject: Permission for study tour Respected Sir, Our school is planning a study tour next week. I would like to participate in this educational trip with my classmates. I kindly request you to grant me permission to join the study tour. Thank you. Yours obediently Raihan Class 10 Roll 5 Example 4: Application from Parents Sometimes schools require permission from parents. To The Principal ABC High School Subject: Permission for my son to join the study tour Respected Sir, I am the father of Raihan, a student of class nine in your school. I have learned that the school is organizing a study tour next week. I am happy to allow my son to participate in this educational trip. I believe it will be a great learning opportunity for him. Thank you for organizing such activities for students. Sinc

title: How to Study Abroad from Bangladesh - Complete Guide 2026
excerpt: Everything a Bangladeshi student needs to know: choosing a country, IELTS requirements, scholarships, the visa process, and what to expect when you arrive.
plainContent: Every year, tens of thousands of Bangladeshi students leave for universities in the UK, Australia, Canada, the United States, Germany, Malaysia, and beyond. Studying abroad opens doors to world-class education, international work experience, and often a pathway to residency in a new country. But the process — from choosing a university to landing at the airport with a student visa in hand — can feel overwhelming if you don't know where to start. This guide walks you through every stage of the journey, step by step, with specific information relevant to students from Bangladesh. Why Study Abroad from Bangladesh? Bangladesh has made enormous strides in its domestic university sector, but studying at a recognized international institution still carries significant advantages for Bangladeshi students: Global degree recognition — Degrees from UK, Australian, Canadian, and American universities are accepted by employers worldwide without question. Post-study work rights — The UK's Graduate Route visa (2 years), Australia's Temporary Graduate visa (2–4 years), and Canada's Post-Graduation Work Permit (up to 3 years) let you gain international work experience after graduating. Pathways to residency — Canada and Australia in particular have structured immigration systems where studying locally can significantly strengthen a permanent residency application. Research and facilities — Access to research labs, libraries, and academic networks that are simply unavailable in Bangladesh for most fields. Personal growth — Language fluency, cultural adaptability, and independence are qualities that employers across every industry increasingly value. Step-by-Step: How to Study Abroad from Bangladesh 1 Decide What You Want to Study and Why Before choosing a country or university, be clear on your field, level (undergraduate or postgraduate), and career goal. Different countries have different strengths — engineering in Germany, business in the UK, healthcare in Australia, technology in Canada. Your choice of field should drive your choice of destination. 2 Check Your Academic Eligibility Most undergraduate programs abroad require your SSC and HSC results. A GPA of 4.00+ in HSC (out of 5.00) is generally competitive. For postgraduate programs, your bachelor's degree transcript is the key document — a CGPA of 3.00+ (out of 4.00) from a recognized Bangladesh university is typically the minimum. Use our HSC GPA Calculator and CGPA Calculator to verify your scores. 3 Take IELTS (or an Accepted Alternative) For English-medium programs in the UK, Australia, Canada, and USA, an English language test is mandatory. IELTS Academic is the most widely accepted. Aim for at least 6.5 overall for most universities. See the IELTS requirements section below for country-by-country details. 4 Research Universities and Programs Use official university websites, QS World University Rankings, and the Times Higher Education rankings. Apply to a range of universities — 2–3 reach schools, 3–4 target schools, and 2 safe options. Pay attention to entry requirements, tuition fees, and scholarship availability for international students. 5 Apply for Scholarships Early Scholarships have earlier deadlines than university applications — sometimes by 3–6 months. Research government scholarships (Chevening, Australia Awards, Commonwealth) and university merit scholarships simultaneously with your applications. 6 Submit University Applications Prepare your Statement of Purpose (SOP), academic transcripts, recommendation letters (usually 2–3), CV, and proof of English proficiency. Deadlines vary — UK universities via UCAS typically close in January for September intake; Australian and Canadian universities often have rolling admissions. 7 Apply for Your Student Visa Once you have a Conditional or Unconditional Offer and have accepted it, you can apply for a student visa. You will need proof of funds (typically covering 1 year of tuition + living costs), your offer letter, IELTS results, and passport photos. Apply at least 3 months before your course start date. 8 Prepare to Depart Arrange student accommodation (university halls or private), open a student bank account in your destination country (many banks let you do this online before arriving), sort travel and health insurance, and attend any pre-departure orientation offered by your university or the Bangladesh embassy. IELTS Score Requirements by Country The IELTS Academic test is required for admission to most English-medium programs abroad. Here are the typical minimum requirements by destination country. Note that individual programs may require higher scores. Country Undergraduate Minimum Postgraduate Minimum No Band Below 🇬🇧 United Kingdom 6.0 overall 6.5 overall 5.5 🇦🇺 Australia 6.0–6.5 overall 6.5 overall 6.0 🇨🇦 Canada 6.0–6.5 overall 6.5–7.0 overall 6.0 🇺🇸 United States 6.5 overall 7.0 overall 6.0 🇩🇪 Germany 6.0 (English programs) 6.5 (English programs) 5.5 🇲🇾 Malaysia

title: About Study Koro
plainContent: Study Koro is a free educational resource built by and for Bangladeshi students. We make academic tools and study guides that are honest, accurate, and easy to use — the kind of resources we wished we had during our own school, college, and university years. What we do We focus on two things: Calculators that implement the official grading rules used in Bangladesh — the Ministry of Education's 5.00 GPA scale for SSC and HSC, the University Grants Commission's 4.00 scale for university CGPA, and the British Council / IDP band rules for IELTS. Guides on the practical questions Bangladeshi students actually search for: how GPA works, how to prepare for IELTS, how to apply to universities abroad, how to write applications and SOPs, and how to navigate scholarships and visas. Why we built it Most academic tools available to Bangladeshi students are either incorrect (using Indian or international grading rules), heavy with ads and pop-ups, or so confusingly designed that students stop trusting the result. We wanted to build something different: simple, fast, accurate, and free — with no account required and no data collected from your inputs. The same applies to our writing. The internet has plenty of generic study-abroad content, but very little written from a Bangladeshi student's perspective with realistic costs, real visa processes, and the specific rules that apply here. We try to fill that gap. How we work Original content. Every guide is written from scratch, not copy-pasted or AI-spun. Verified against official sources. Grading rules, scholarship details, and visa requirements are checked against official board, UGC, embassy, and university documents — and updated when those rules change. No paywalls, no signups. Every tool and every guide is free to use. Privacy-first. Calculator inputs stay in your browser. We don't collect or store the marks, grades, or scores you enter. Editorial standards When we publish a guide, we follow three rules: Useful before clever. Concrete numbers, real examples, and step-by-step instructions instead of motivational filler. Honest about limits. If a topic has exceptions, official ambiguity, or genuine risk, we say so. Updated when reality changes. Visa rules, scholarship deadlines, and university requirements shift constantly. We revisit our guides and date every meaningful change. Who runs Study Koro Study Koro is run by a small group of Bangladeshi graduates with backgrounds in engineering, education, and editorial work. We've been through the SSC, HSC, university CGPA, and IELTS process ourselves, and several of our contributors have gone through study-abroad applications to the UK, Australia, and Germany. Get in touch Found an error? Want a topic covered? Have a suggestion for a new calculator? We genuinely want to hear from you — see our contact page for how to reach us.

title: University CGPA Calculator
plainContent: Semester-wise GPA tracking and cumulative CGPA calculation for all Bangladesh universities. Includes target GPA planner. Current semester courses Course name Credit hours Grade Add course No courses added yet. Previous semesters (optional) Add your completed semesters to get a cumulative CGPA. Semester GPA Credits Add semester Target CGPA planner Target CGPA Remaining credits How this calculator works Bangladesh follows the University Grants Commission (UGC) 4.00 scale: A+ = 4.00, A = 3.75, A− = 3.50, B+ = 3.25, B = 3.00, B− = 2.75, C+ = 2.50, C = 2.25, D = 2.00, F = 0.00. Unlike SSC and HSC, university CGPA is credit-weighted — each course is multiplied by its credits, summed, and divided by total credits attempted. The target GPA planner tells you what semester GPA you need to reach a future CGPA goal, given your current CGPA and completed credits. How to use it Enter each course's credits and the letter grade you received. Add as many courses or semesters as needed — the calculator tracks cumulative totals. Use the target-GPA planner to enter your goal CGPA and remaining credits, and the calculator tells you the required semester GPA. Frequently asked questions Why is my university CGPA out of 4 and not 5? Bangladeshi universities follow the UGC standard, which uses a 4.00 scale. SSC and HSC use a separate 5.00 scale set by the Ministry of Education. How is CGPA different from semester GPA? Semester GPA is for one semester only. CGPA is the credit-weighted average across all semesters you have completed. Does the calculator handle retakes? Most universities replace the lower grade with the higher one. If your university uses this rule, only enter the retake grade — not both attempts. What CGPA is considered good in Bangladesh? 3.50+ is strong, 3.00–3.49 is solid, below 3.00 limits scholarship and job options. For study abroad, 3.25+ is often the practical floor. Can I convert CGPA to percentage with this tool? The result page shows an approximate percentage. For an in-depth explanation, read our CGPA-to-percentage guide linked below.

title: HSC GPA Calculator
plainContent: Calculate your HSC GPA online using your subject marks or letter grades. This free HSC GPA Calculator supports Science, Business Studies, and Humanities students in Bangladesh and automatically applies the applicable 4th-subject bonus . Enter your marks or grades below to calculate your estimated GPA, total grade points, and equivalent percentage. Group Science Business Studies Humanities Main subjects Enter a letter grade OR marks. Marks fields take the total out of 200 (out of 100 for ICT). Optional subject (4th subject bonus) Optional subject Calculate GPA Reset Note: This calculator provides an estimate based on the Bangladesh HSC grading system. Your official GPA is the result shown on the marksheet issued by the relevant education board. HSC GPA Calculator Bangladesh 2026 The HSC GPA Calculator helps students estimate their Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) Grade Point Average from their subject results. You can enter either your letter grades or your marks . The calculator converts your marks into the corresponding grade points and calculates your overall GPA. It supports the three main HSC groups: Science Business Studies Humanities The calculator also supports the 4th or optional subject , allowing the applicable bonus to be included automatically. If you already have your marks or grades, enter them above to get your estimated HSC GPA. How to Calculate HSC GPA Bangladesh's HSC grading system uses a 5.00-point scale . Each subject result is converted into a letter grade and corresponding grade point. For example: 80–100 marks = A+ = 5.00 70–79 marks = A = 4.00 60–69 marks = A− = 3.50 50–59 marks = B = 3.00 40–49 marks = C = 2.00 33–39 marks = D = 1.00 0–32 marks = F = 0.00 The official Education Board grading table uses this marks-to-grade-point scale. For the main subjects, the grade points are used to determine the student's GPA. If an optional or 4th subject is included, the applicable bonus is added according to the grading rules. Simple example Suppose a student receives these grade points: Subject Grade Grade Point Bangla A+ 5.00 English A 4.00 ICT A+ 5.00 Physics A+ 5.00 Chemistry A 4.00 Biology A+ 5.00 The grade points from the main subjects are used to calculate the student's GPA. If the student also has an optional subject, the 4th-subject rule is applied before the final GPA is determined. HSC Grading System in Bangladesh The HSC grading system uses a 5.00 GPA scale. The following table shows the standard marks-to-grade conversion used by Bangladesh's Education Boards. Marks Letter Grade Grade Point 80–100 A+ 5.00 70–79 A 4.00 60–69 A− 3.50 50–59 B 3.00 40–49 C 2.00 33–39 D 1.00 0–32 F 0.00 What do the grades mean? A+ (5.00) The highest grade point on the HSC grading scale. A (4.00) A strong result with a grade point of 4.00. A− (3.50) A grade point of 3.50. B (3.00) A grade point of 3.00. C (2.00) A grade point of 2.00. D (1.00) The minimum passing grade. F (0.00) A failing grade in the subject. HSC 4th Subject Bonus: How Does It Work? The 4th subject, also called the optional subject , is treated differently from the main subjects. When the grade point earned in the optional subject is above 2.00 , the amount above 2.00 is treated as the bonus. For example: Optional subject grade point = 5.00 Then: 5.00 − 2.00 = 3.00 bonus points Similarly: Optional subject grade point = 4.00 4.00 − 2.00 = 2.00 bonus points And: Optional subject grade point = 3.50 3.50 − 2.00 = 1.50 bonus points The bonus is then incorporated into the overall GPA calculation according to the applicable HSC rules. Our calculator applies the 4th-subject calculation automatically, so you do not need to calculate the bonus manually. HSC GPA Calculator for Science Students Science students can use this calculator to estimate their HSC GPA by entering their marks or grades for their compulsory and group-specific subjects. Depending on the student's subject combination, the group subjects may include: Physics Chemistry Biology Higher Mathematics Select Science in the calculator and enter the appropriate results for your subjects. If you have an optional subject, enter it separately in the 4th Subject field so that the applicable bonus can be included. Example A Science student might enter: Subject Result Bangla A+ English A ICT A+ Physics A+ Chemistry A Biology A+ 4th Subject A+ The calculator will process the grade points and show the estimated GPA. HSC GPA Calculator for Business Studies Students Business Studies students can also calculate their HSC GPA using the calculator. Select Business Studies and enter the marks or grades for your subjects. Depending on the student's subject combination, group-specific subjects can include areas such as: Accounting Finance, Banking and Insurance Business Organization and Management Economics or another approved subject Your exact subject combination may vary, so use the subjects shown on your own HSC registration or marksheet. title: IELTS Band Score Calculator
plainContent: Calculate your overall IELTS band for Academic and General Training. Convert raw Listening and Reading scores to band scores. Module Academic General Training Listening & Reading Enter your raw score out of 40 - the band is converted automatically. Listening raw score (0-40) Band: - Reading raw score (0-40) Band: - Writing & Speaking Writing band Speaking band How this calculator works The calculator implements the official IELTS band conversion rules from the British Council / IDP. For Listening, raw scores out of 40 map to band scores using a fixed table; the same applies to Reading, but the conversion differs between Academic and General Training. Writing and Speaking are entered directly as half-band scores. The overall band is the average of the four section scores, rounded using IELTS's standard rule: averages ending in .25 round up to the next half-band; averages ending in .75 round up to the next whole band. How to use it Choose Academic or General Training module. Enter your raw Listening score (out of 40) — the calculator converts it to a band. Enter your raw Reading score (out of 40). Enter your Writing and Speaking band scores (in 0.5 increments). Read your overall band and section breakdown. Frequently asked questions Is the Reading conversion really different for Academic and General? Yes. The General Training Reading test is easier, so it requires more correct answers to achieve the same band. For example, 30/40 is roughly Band 7.0 in Academic but Band 6.0 in General. How is the overall band calculated? Add the four section band scores and divide by four. If the average ends in .25, round up to the next half-band; if it ends in .75, round up to the next whole band. What band do I need to study abroad? UK and Australia typically require 6.0–6.5 overall with no band below 5.5–6.0. Scholarships often require 7.0+. Is the Listening conversion the same on every test? The official conversion table is fixed, but individual test versions are equated so difficulty is comparable. The calculator uses the standard published table. Are these results official? No. Only your Test Report Form (TRF) issued by the British Council or IDP is official. This is an estimate to plan your preparation.

title: SSC GPA Calculator
plainContent: Calculate your SSC GPA for Science, Commerce, and Arts groups across all Bangladesh education boards. Uses official grading rules. Group Science Commerce Arts / Humanities Entry mode Letter grade Marks (0-100) Core subjects 4th subject (bonus) Grade points above C (2.00) in the 4th subject are added to your total, up to a maximum GPA of 5.00. Calculate GPA Reset How this calculator works This calculator follows the official grading scale of the Bangladesh Education Boards: A+ = 5.00, A = 4.00, A− = 3.50, B = 3.00, C = 2.00, D = 1.00, F = 0.00. Your SSC GPA is the average of the grade points of your main subjects. The 4th-subject rule is applied automatically — if your 4th-subject grade point is greater than 2.00, the excess (grade point minus 2.00) is added to your total before averaging. If you fail any subject (F), the overall GPA is 0.00 regardless of the others. How to use it Select your group (Science, Commerce, or Arts). Enter the letter grade or marks for each main subject. Enter the grade for your 4th subject (the bonus is applied automatically). Read your GPA, total grade points, and equivalent percentage from the result card. Frequently asked questions Is the 4th-subject bonus applied automatically? Yes. If your 4th-subject grade point is greater than 2.00, the excess is added to your total grade points before averaging — exactly as the boards calculate it. What is the highest SSC GPA possible? GPA 5.00 — sometimes called GPA 5 with Golden A+, which means you scored A+ in every subject including the 4th subject. What happens if I fail one subject? If you receive an F in any subject, the official rule is that your overall GPA becomes 0.00 — you must retake that subject to clear the SSC certificate. Does this calculator work for Madrasah and Technical boards? The grading scale is the same. The main subject list may differ, so use the closest matching group and update subject names as needed. Is this an official result? No. This is an estimate based on the official grading rules. Your real GPA is whatever the education board issues on your marksheet.
